headline: Bitcoin ETF outflows accelerate as institutional capital eyes Anthropic's Nasdaq debut
summary: The dominant story today isn't price — Bitcoin barely moved, slipping 0.14% to $63,409 — it's where institutional money is going. Sustained ETF outflows signal that large allocators are rotating toward the Anthropic IPO and broader equities, leaving crypto in a holding pattern with the Fear & Greed index at an extreme-fear reading of 10. Meanwhile, two major security stories landed: Binance secured a $6.5 billion asset freeze against hackers behind the largest crypto theft on record, and revelations emerged that North Korean state actors exploited Sky's stablecoin infrastructure, putting billions of dollars in assets at potential freeze risk.

winners.name: Hyperliquid
winners.catalyst: 1inch integrated Hyperliquid's perpetual futures contracts into its dApp and wallet platform, expanding the protocol's distribution to a much broader user base and driving positive sentiment at a time when most assets were flat.

losers.name: Rain
losers.catalyst: No clear catalyst identified — the move appears technical against a backdrop of broad risk-off sentiment and extreme fear readings across the market.

whyItMoved:
Price action today was nearly flat across the board — Bitcoin's -0.14% slip and Ethereum's +1.21% gain are both within the noise of a quiet session. The Fear & Greed index sitting at 10 (extreme fear) tells the real story: institutional appetite for crypto has cooled sharply, and the mechanism is visible in the ETF data. Sustained outflows from Bitcoin ETFs this week reflect large allocators rotating capital toward the Anthropic IPO and equities more broadly. When a high-profile AI company lists on Nasdaq, it competes directly for the same pool of risk capital that flows into crypto — and right now, equities are winning that competition.

The security headlines added to the cautious tone without triggering a sharp selloff, which itself says something about how numb the market has become to bad news. Binance's $6.5 billion asset freeze against hackers behind the largest crypto theft on record is a genuine legal milestone — it demonstrates that exchanges can pursue meaningful recovery through courts — but it didn't move prices. The North Korean state-actor story involving Sky's stablecoin infrastructure is more structurally significant: if billions in assets face freeze risk due to sanctions exposure, that raises real questions about DeFi stablecoin protocols and the counterparty risks embedded in them.

Hyperliquid was the one clear outlier, gaining 2.73% after 1inch announced it would integrate Hyperliquid's perpetual futures (contracts that let traders bet on price direction without holding the underlying asset) into its platform — a distribution win that brought the protocol to a much wider audience on a day when most assets went nowhere.
worthKnowing: Binance secured a $6.5 billion court-ordered asset freeze against hackers responsible for the largest crypto theft on record, a rare legal win for exchange-led recovery efforts.

North Korean state-linked actors were found to have exploited Sky's stablecoin infrastructure, raising systemic freeze risk for billions in assets and drawing fresh regulatory scrutiny toward DeFi stablecoin protocols.

Singapore's Monetary Authority settled a $77.5 million tokenized government bill sale using its local central bank digital currency, one of the largest real-world tests of blockchain-based sovereign debt issuance to date.
